query: What distinct aspects of food quality do reviewers focus on?

per_column.name: facet_taste
per_column.rationale: Taste is a core food-quality axis directly answering the query; flags in samples (taffy, confection 'very flavorful', 'medicinal flavor') are well grounded. Dog food row correctly 0.

per_column.name: facet_texture
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis. Confection 'light, pillowy... not too chewy' correctly flagged 1; other rows correctly 0. Sound readings.

per_column.name: facet_freshness
per_column.rationale: Legitimate quality facet; all sampled rows are 0, consistent with texts that do not mention freshness. Reasonable silence handling.

per_column.name: facet_smell_aroma
per_column.rationale: Valid distinct axis. Dog food text explicitly says 'it smells better' yet flagged 0 — a missed positive, minor grounding lapse, but not an invented value.

per_column.name: facet_appearance
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis. Dog food 'looks more like a stew' reasonably maps to appearance=1. Peanuts 'small sized' size mismatch arguably appearance but left 0; defensible.

per_column.name: facet_ingredients_nutrition
per_column.rationale: Useful axis, but flagging tends to be loose: confection with 'nuts' and cherry soda with 'secret ingredient' get 1, which is stretched — closer to flavor than nutrition. Somewhat overextended mapping.

per_column.name: facet_packaging_quantity
per_column.rationale: Relevant axis but very high positive rate (4834) and questionable calls: taffy row flagged 1 with only 'price'/'delivery' mentioned, not packaging/quantity. Peanuts row (mislabeled size) plausibly qualifies yet is 0. Inconsistent grounding.

per_column.name: facet_consistency_brand
per_column.rationale: Conflates two loosely related notions (consistency, brand), weakening interpretability, but still a usable axis. Sampled 0s are consistent with texts.

per_column.name: primary_quality_facet
per_column.rationale: Single-label roll-up is highly useful for grouping the query. Grounding mostly reasonable, but inherits weaker facet calls (e.g., confection labeled 'ingredients_nutrition' over the stronger taste/texture signals) and taffy 'packaging_quantity' from a shaky flag.

judge.rationale: The added columns decompose food quality into genuinely distinct, query-relevant facets (taste, texture, freshness, smell, appearance, ingredients, packaging, consistency/brand) plus a primary-facet roll-up, giving strong analytical leverage for 'what aspects reviewers focus on' with real grouping and comparison power. None are near-constant restatements of original columns. Grounding is generally sound with correct silence handling, but several flags are loose or overextended (packaging_quantity flagged from price/delivery mentions, ingredients_nutrition stretched to include flavor/nuts, and a missed explicit 'smells better' signal), which mildly depresses groundedness. Judged only on usefulness and groundedness, the set passes both necessary conditions.
